chapter: Chicago in the 1950s: Mercury, unions and jobbing
title: The NBC executive and Petrillo's union
summary: An NBC executive tells Hodes he cannot hire five men when he has 95. Hodes says the union made work for a few.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And so I discovered this about the recording business. But we had all sorts of experiences of going up to the agency and asking me again, what else do you do, we know you play, but what else? I have a friend who's got a vice president of NBC, he's a tremendous friend of him, he owes him a favor. And this guy is a real good friend of mine.

T2 52 Ya bum, you shouldn't be out of work, I'll meet you tomorrow and drive you to the city. We'll go up to NBC, go up to NBC, man comes out of conference and talks to us. He is a friend of my friend. He says to me, Art, what can you do with your five men that I couldn't pull five men out of the 95 that Petrillo says I've got to have, and approximate what you're doing? If not do the same thing.

Honestly, I can't say no to that. He says, now, why should I go buy five more men, when I'm fortunate to have 95? So this was the other side of the thing. The union was making some musicians a lot of work and a lot of money. The few were
getting it all, the many, scraping for what was left on the bottom.
Same story. So this was the Chicago scene that I was involved in. And -- which brings me to the time I finally looked at my hands and said, what am I doing, and I started teaching.
